In [[geometry]], the '''square gyrobicupola''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|29}}}}). Like the [[square orthobicupola]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|28}}}}), it can be obtained by joining two [[square cupola]]e ({{math|''J''{{sub|4}}}}) along their bases. The difference is that in this solid, the two halves are rotated 45 degrees with respect to one another.

{{Johnson solid}}

The ''square gyrobicupola'' is the second in an infinite set of [[Bicupola (geometry)|gyrobicupolae]].

Related to the square gyrobicupola is the [[elongated square gyrobicupola]]. This polyhedron is created when an [[octagonal prism]] is inserted between the two halves of the square gyrobicupola.
[[File:J29 square gyrobicupola.stl|thumb|3D model of a square gyrobicupola]]

==Formulae==
The following [[formula]]e for [[volume]] and [[surface area]] can be used if all [[face (geometry)|faces]] are [[regular polygon|regular]], with edge length ''a'':<ref>[[Stephen Wolfram]], "[http://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=Triangular+gyrobicupola Triangular gyrobicupola]" from [[Wolfram Alpha]]. Retrieved July 23, 2010.</ref>

:<math>V=\left(2+\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)a^3\approx3.88562...a^3</math>

:<math>A=2\left(5+\sqrt{3}\right)a^2\approx13.4641...a^2</math>

==Related polyhedra and honeycombs==

The square gyrobicupola forms space-filling [[Honeycomb (geometry)|honeycomb]]s with [[Tetrahedron|tetrahedra]], [[cube]]s and [[Cuboctahedron|cuboctahedra]]; and with tetrahedra, [[square pyramid]]s, and  [[elongated square bipyramid]]s. (The latter unit can be decomposed into [[elongated square pyramid]]s, cubes, and/or square pyramids).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://woodenpolyhedra.web.fc2.com/J29.html|title = J29 honeycomb}}</ref><br>
